claims.claim: The repository ships 283 restaurants and 312 visits extracted from two food bloggers' public Weibo posts.
claims.metric: number of restaurant records and visit records in the committed restaurants.json files
claims.method: counted directly from data/陈晓卿/restaurants.json (252 restaurants) and data/隋坡/restaurants.json (31 restaurants); a visit is one entry in a restaurant's visits array, each carrying its source Weibo post URL

check.cmd: node -e "const f=n=>require('./data/'+n+'/restaurants.json');const a=[...f('陈晓卿'),...f('隋坡')];const v=a.flatMap(r=>r.visits);console.log(a.length, v.length, require('./data/bloggers.json').length)"

claims.claim: That dataset is predominantly Chinese: 262 of the 283 restaurants are in China, spread over 3 continents, 8 countries or regions and 95 cities or districts in total.
claims.value: 262/283 in China; 3 continents, 8 countries or regions, 95 cities or districts
claims.metric: distinct values of the continent / country / city fields of the location object across the committed restaurant records
claims.method: the location object is written by geocode-regions.mjs, which reverse-geocodes each restaurant's own coordinates through Nominatim, so the region reflects where the restaurant is rather than where the blogger was posting from
claims.repro: node -e "const f=n=>require('./data/'+n+'/restaurants.json');const a=[...f('陈晓卿'),...f('隋坡')];const g=k=>new Set(a.map(r=>(r.location||{})[k]).filter(Boolean));console.log(g('continent').size,g('country').size,g('city').size,a.filter(r=>(r.location||{}).country==='中国').length)"

claims.claim: Every visit record links back to the public Weibo post it was extracted from.
claims.metric: share of visit records containing a non-empty postUrl field
claims.method: extract.mjs keeps the source post id, URL, date and a quoted excerpt on each visit, so any recommendation on the map can be checked against the blogger's own public post instead of being taken on trust

claims.claim: The live demo's per-blogger totals are 252 restaurants / 281 visits for Chen Xiaoqing (陈晓卿) and 31 restaurants / 31 visits for Sui Po (隋坡).
claims.value: 陈晓卿 252 restaurants / 281 visits; 隋坡 31 restaurants / 31 visits
claims.metric: length of each committed data/<blogger>/restaurants.json, and the total length of the visits arrays inside it
claims.method: each blogger has exactly one committed restaurants.json, so the per-blogger figure is that file's own record count and visit count; the two files sum to the 283 / 312 repository total, and data/bloggers.json lists the two names the dropdown switches between

claims.claim: Restaurant dedup merges two spellings only when one name is a substring of the other and the coordinates are within 500m (e.g. "柴氏" / "甘家口柴氏"); the threshold lives in extract.mjs.
claims.metric: the value of the distance threshold used by mergeNearbyAliases, converted to metres
claims.method: mergeNearbyAliases() in extract.mjs skips the merge when the spherical distance between the two points exceeds ALIAS_MAX_DISTANCE_KM, declared as 0.5 km at the top of the file; the check parses that declaration out of the source and converts it to metres, so the README's "within 500m" rule is pinned to the code that implements it

claims.claim: Only posts carrying an official location (geo) tag or a check-in card are collected; the author's local scrape of the Chen Xiaoqing account measured a hit rate of about 18% (1131 of 6129 original posts).
claims.metric: share of the blogger's original posts carrying a location signal
claims.method: measured by the author's local raw scrape of the Chen Xiaoqing profile feed; posts without a geo field or a check-in card are dropped before extraction, so this ratio is a property of the raw feed rather than of the committed dataset
claims.repro: cannot be run here: it needs data/陈晓卿/posts_raw.json, which .gitignore excludes (data/*/posts_raw.json)

check.manual: Neither the 6129 original posts nor the 1131 of them that carry a location signal exist in the repository: the raw scrape data/<blogger>/posts_raw.json is gitignored (.gitignore: data/*/posts_raw.json) and only the post-extraction restaurants.json is committed, so no committed artifact can recompute the ratio. What is missing is a committed copy of the raw feed, or at least a committed per-post location-signal count derived from it — the same caveat the README states verbatim.

claims.claim: The only committed measurement of the geo hit rate is normalize.mjs's own probe: 13 of 25 posts (≈52%) on a 25-post sample of a test account (2026-07).
claims.metric: share of sampled posts whose geo field parses, on the probe sample recorded in normalize.mjs
claims.method: recorded as a field finding in the normalize.mjs header comment (sample of a test account, 2026-07); parseGeo() is the function that decides whether a post counts as a hit
claims.repro: cannot be run here: only the resulting 13/25 figure is committed (in normalize.mjs's comment), not the 25 posts it was measured on

check.manual: The probe requires the raw posts of the test account it was run against; those posts are not committed (the repository ships no posts_raw.json at all — .gitignore excludes data/*/posts_raw.json — and the account is a live Weibo test account that nothing in the repo can reach). What is missing is the 25-post sample, or a committed fixture of it, from which parseGeo() could be re-run.

claims.metric: the restaurant and visit counts rendered in the committed screenshot

claims.repro: cannot be run here: the 264 / 285 figures live in the pixels of a committed image, not in any committed data file

What is missing is either the dataset snapshot the image was captured from or an OCR step able to read the numbers back out of the PNG.

claims.claim: Every page in this repository that animates also handles `prefers-reduced-motion` — motion here is decoration, so the page must stay readable and complete when it is off.
claims.value: no animated page without a reduced-motion branch
claims.method: the check walks every committed .html page, and where it finds an animation it requires a reduced-motion branch. It does not judge what the fallback does — only that one exists, because a missing branch is invisible in review and obvious to the person who gets motion sickness.

check.cmd:
python3 - <<'PY'
import pathlib, re

pages = [p for p in list(pathlib.Path('.').glob('*.html')) + list(pathlib.Path('.').glob('docs/*.html'))
         if p.name != 'template.html']
animated, missing = 0, []
for p in pages:
    t = p.read_text(encoding='utf-8', errors='replace')
    if re.search(r'animation\s*:|@keyframes', t):
        animated += 1
        if 'prefers-reduced-motion' not in t:
            missing.append(p.name)
print('pages', len(pages), 'animated', animated, 'missing', missing)
assert not missing
PY
